edible_parts: Seeds, roasted; the flesh is bitter and inedible.
other_uses: Known from a handful of collections in Oaxaca, Mexico. One of the least-known species in the genus — undomesticated, and possibly of conservation concern.
prep: Split the hard gourds, wash the seeds free of pulp, dry and roast them — they are oily and protein-rich. The flesh is not eaten. Saponin-rich fruit and roots lather in water and were used as soap.
harvest: Gourds ripen and dry on the vine in autumn; seeds keep for years.
risks: Flesh, fruit and root are loaded with bitter cucurbitacins — strongly purgative and toxic in quantity. Only the roasted seeds are food.
